newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA says strike won't hit Venezuela oil output.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA says strike won't hit Venezuela oil output.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said on Thursday a national strike called for August 6 would have no impact on oil production.

The 11-hour stoppage was called by the country's biggest trade union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), in protest at Thursday's hike in gasoline prices and delays in the payment of private-sector salary rises.
Carlos Ortega, president of the main oil workers' union Fedepetrol, said some 60,000 oil workers would join the nationwide action.

"PDVSA has a contingency plan. When strikes occur, senior management takes over duties to ensure continued production. This has happened several times before and never affected production," a PDVSA spokeswoman said.
Venezuela is the world's seventh biggest oil producer with about 3.2 million barrels of daily output.
Fedepetrol is threatening a separate strike in protest at restructuring at PDVSA, which it says threatens 12,000 jobs. Ortega is due to meet the government next week to discuss the changes.
